subject: Plain-language subprocessor & cross-border blurb for hosted API console (Acme)
messages:
From: Sam Hart <sam.hart@acme.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short/plain-language subprocessor + cross-border note for our privacy page

Hi Vanessa / Laura —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Acme's legal & privacy teams asked for a one- or two-sentence blurb we can put in our vendor list and privacy page that explains: (1) who your subprocessors are at a high level, (2) whether customer data for hosted API calls can leave the EEA, and (3) where to find the full subprocessor list.

High-level constraints from our side: we need something non-legal that our product/privacy teams can paste into a customer-facing page (not a DPA). It must avoid definitive promises that data "will never" transfer outside the EEA, but should be reassuring and point to controls (data region, encryption, SCCs, subprocessors list).

Do you have a draft we could review? Ideally short (<= 2 sentences) + link to full list. Also, if possible, attach your current subprocessor CSV so our team can validate.

Thanks —
Sam
Sam Hart
Senior Privacy Counsel, Acme Corp
sam.hart@acme.com

---
Note: Acme will be publishing vendor blurbs in its partner directory on Nov 1st, so a quick turnaround would help.

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Request: short/plain-language subprocessor + cross-border note for our privacy page

Sam —

Thanks for the clear ask. Draft below (first pass) plus attached current subprocessor map. I tried to keep it simple and non-legal while surfacing the controls Acme cares about. Please let me know if you'd prefer slightly stronger or softer language.

Draft (v1):
"Redwood Inference works with a limited set of trusted subprocessors (infrastructure, logging, and analytics). For customers that choose hosted API, data may be processed in the EEA and additional regions; when data crosses borders we rely on standard transfer safeguards (SCCs and other protections). See our full subprocessor list and details here: https://redwood.com/subprocessors."

Notes: 1) I avoided claiming "data never leaves" and included SCCs. 2) If legal wants an explicit note about hosting regions / residency toggle, we can add a parenthetical. 3) Attachment: subprocessor-map-2026Q3.csv

Attachments: subprocessor-map-2026Q3.csv (CSV: vendor, service, region)

Would love a quick read from Kim on whether we need any qualifiers. Laura — FYI for console placement (small help text vs. dedicated modal).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: Request: short/plain-language subprocessor + cross-border note for our privacy page

Thanks Vanessa — nice concise draft. A few quick legal redlines to keep it safe for customer-facing content:

1) Replace "data may be processed in the EEA and additional regions" with "processing may occur in the EEA and other regions" (more neutral).
2) Add a short clause about safeguards: "We apply appropriate safeguards such as SCCs, encryption in transit, and contractual controls." Avoid implying a specific legal mechanism is always used (e.g., "we rely on SCCs" could be read as exclusive).

Suggested redlined snippet (v2):
"Redwood Inference uses a limited set of trusted subprocessors to operate our hosted API (infrastructure, logging, analytics). Processing of hosted-api requests may occur in the EEA and other regions; where data is transferred outside the EEA we apply appropriate safeguards such as Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), encryption in transit, and contractual controls. See our full subprocessor list and details here: https://redwood.com/subprocessors."

I attached a quick doc with the redlined language and a one-line rationale per change. If Acme's privacy team wants something even simpler, we can create a 1-sentence variant that points to the link and omits the safeguards line.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

Sam —

Thanks for the patience. Per Kim's redlines and a quick product check with Laura/Rishi, here's the agreed public-facing blurb you can publish in Acme's partner directory or privacy page:

Final public blurb (publishable):
"Redwood Inference works with a limited set of trusted subprocessors to operate our hosted API (infrastructure, logging, and analytics). Processing of hosted-api requests may occur in the EEA and other regions; where data is transferred outside the EEA we apply appropriate safeguards such as Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), encryption in transit, and contractual controls.
